sources.title: Air Fryers and Food Safety
sources.publisher: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service

chunks.text: Air-fryer time and temperature vary by appliance and food. Check food with a thermometer. USDA lists 145 degrees Fahrenheit as the safe minimum internal temperature for fish.
Do not overfill an air-fryer basket because restricted hot-air circulation can cause uneven cooking and undercooking. Cook larger amounts in batches.

sources.title: Selecting and Serving Fresh and Frozen Seafood Safely

chunks.text: FDA says most seafood should reach an internal temperature of 145 degrees Fahrenheit. Visual texture may help assess doneness, but a thermometer supplies the temperature measurement.
Frozen seafood can spoil if it thaws and remains warm too long. A photograph cannot recover an unknown cold-chain history or establish that frozen seafood stayed at a safe temperature.

sources.title: Agentic Salmon Evidence and Authority Policy

chunks.text: Visible skin can support the hypothesis that the portions are fish, but an image without original packaging cannot verify species, ingredients, allergens, freshness, storage history, or food safety.

Reason may propose bounded guidance while retaining unknown identity and cold-chain history. Act remains unavailable until a human explicitly accepts the uncertainty and authorizes the bounded response.
